lab_title: Human Heart Anatomy and Blood Flow Pathway
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart and the four major valves.
Trace the path of blood through the heart and major connecting vessels.
Explain the difference between pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Describe how valve function and ventricular wall thickness support one-way blood flow and pumping demands.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart as a muscular pump and orient students to its overall shape and major surface landmarks before they study internal structures.
key_visuals: A realistic 3D heart model in anterior view with clear left/right orientation
Visible great vessels emerging from the top of the heart
Subtle highlight labels for the apex, base, and major external vessels
student_actions: Rotate the heart to recognize its front, back, top, and bottom.
Identify the sides of the heart and locate the major vessels entering and leaving it.
Select the heart’s apex and base to confirm overall orientation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students locate and distinguish the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle as the main receiving and pumping chambers.
key_visuals: A cutaway heart view exposing the four chambers
Distinct shading or outlining for each chamber to emphasize spatial relationships
Text labels anchored near each chamber
student_actions: Tap each chamber to reveal its name and function.
Compare the size and wall thickness of the left and right ventricles.
Match each atrium with the ventricle below it on the same side.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how the heart’s valves separate chambers and prevent backflow during contraction.
key_visuals: Opened internal heart view with the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves highlighted
Simple motion cues showing valves opening and closing
Directional arrows indicating forward blood movement
student_actions: Identify each valve by location between chambers or at vessel exits.
Follow the opening and closing sequence as the heart cycles.
Explain which valves keep blood from moving backward after contraction.

scenes.scene_name: From Body to Lungs: Right Heart and Pulmonary Circuit
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood returning from the body through the right side of the heart and to the lungs.
key_visuals: Flow arrows entering the superior and inferior vena cava and moving through the right atrium and ventricle
Highlighted pulmonary arteries leaving the heart toward the lungs
Color contrast showing deoxygenated blood as it moves through the right heart
student_actions: Trace the blood path from the body to the right atrium, right ventricle, and pulmonary arteries.
Name the vessels that bring blood into the right atrium and out toward the lungs.
Order the steps of pulmonary circulation on a guided pathway.

scenes.scene_name: From Lungs to Body: Left Heart and Systemic Circuit
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace oxygenated blood returning from the lungs through the left side of the heart and out to the body via the aorta.
key_visuals: Pulmonary veins entering the left atrium and flowing into the left ventricle
Aortic valve and aorta emphasized as the main خروج pathway to systemic circulation
A stronger-looking left ventricle wall to signal greater pumping force
student_actions: Follow the oxygenated blood path from the lungs to the left atrium and left ventricle.
Identify the pulmonary veins and aorta as key vessels in this circuit.
Compare the left ventricle’s wall thickness with the right ventricle and infer why it is thicker.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate chamber, valve, and vessel knowledge into the complete blood flow sequence through the heart and the two circulatory loops.
key_visuals: A complete heart flow diagram with arrows showing the full route through chambers, valves, and vessels
Side-by-side pulmonary and systemic circulation loops
Summary callouts for backflow prevention and ventricular workload
student_actions: Reconstruct the entire blood flow pathway in the correct order.
Answer a brief check of chamber, valve, and vessel identification.
Explain in one or two sentences how the heart supports both pulmonary and systemic circulation.
